body:
Three self-contained ports from lean-workspace-template:

- **popover.inline.ts** (`4fb49d25`, `660add27`): cache popovers by the hashless/searchless fetch URL instead of `link.pathname` — fixes stale/wrong previews when two links share a pathname but differ by hash or query (common on citation-heavy pages) — plus in-flight fetch race guards, null-safe `Content-Type`, and deduped mouseenter bindings. Canvas-specific styling from the source commits deliberately not ported.
- **config-loader** (`5ca879f7`, `b28ad09f`): a plugin's `layout` may now be an array, so one component can render in multiple responsive placements (search: standalone mobile row + grouped desktop slot). Includes the regression test wired into `test-scripts.yml`, static imports replacing inline `require()`s, the `layoutDeclaration` schema `$defs`, and the matching mobile-search selector in `custom.scss`.
- **.gitignore** (`94525b72`): ignore `.env`/`.env.*` (keep `!.env.example`) — local secrets were previously committable. Plus `checkout@v5`/`setup-node@v5`.

- **Landing page + mobile nav bar** (second commit; lean `bfbac6b5`, `260ea2b1`, and the config half of `5ca879f7`): the landing card now shares every other page's width and top alignment — capped content column with a flexible right spacer replaces the index-only 85%-centered layout — and search/darkmode declare array-form placements, activating the loader mechanism above so the mobile nav renders search on its own row and the theme toggle standalone.

Verified locally: `npm run check`, the new loader test, and a full site build all pass.

**Stack 5/5.**

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #49 ports several Quartz fixes from `lean-workspace-template`: popover cache-key/race handling, array-form plugin layouts, and `.env` ignore hardening. It updates the loader type/schema/test coverage so a component can render in multiple responsive placements. It also changes the landing page/mobile nav layout so search and darkmode can appear differently on mobile and desktop. The PR body reports `npm run check`, the new loader test, and a full build passing; no parent or tracking issue was referenced.

## Review
Overall, reviewers found the implementation scoped and consistent with existing Quartz extension points, with no blocking defects. The only unresolved concerns are verification/coverage notes, not confirmed code defects.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Responsive duplicate search/darkmode placements need runtime verification | WARNING | `search` and `darkmode` now render in separate mobile and desktop placements, so both DOM instances can coexist while CSS hides one. One reviewer flagged singleton DOM wiring risk; another found no blocker and reported check/build/focused test passing. |
| Quartz CI coverage remains narrower than existing tests | INFO | The new workflow step runs only `quartz/plugins/loader/config-loader.test.mjs`, leaving four existing Quartz tests outside this workflow. This is a coverage improvement opportunity, not a merge blocker. |

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Responsive duplicate search/darkmode placements need runtime verification</summary>

**Cause:** The new array-form layout declares separate mobile and desktop placements for the same search and darkmode plugins, producing duplicate live DOM instances gated by responsive display classes.

**Candidate solutions:** Verify both mobile and desktop search open/close, keyboard navigation, dismissal, and darkmode toggling at runtime. If duplicated instances conflict, adjust the component wiring for multiple instances or avoid duplicate DOM for singleton-style components.

**Comments:** This is a runtime confidence issue rather than a proven defect; reviewers disagreed on severity because static checks and focused tests passed.

</details>

<summary>Quartz CI coverage remains narrower than existing tests</summary>

**Cause:** The PR adds a Quartz test step but targets only the new loader test, while existing Quartz tests for search, file trie, path, and Sepo comments remain unwired.

**Candidate solutions:** Keep the focused test if intentionally scoped, or broaden the workflow with an explicit Quartz-only test list after confirming those tests pass in CI.

**Comments:** This is optional coverage hardening; no reviewer identified a current failing behavior.

</details>
